questions.question:
Which of the statements about the reaction below are incorrect?
2PbO(s) + C(s) → 2Pb(s) + CO₂(g)
(a) Lead is getting reduced.
(b) Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised.
(c) Carbon is getting oxidised.
(d) Lead oxide is getting reduced.
options: (i) (a) and (b)
(ii) (a) and (c)
(iii) (a), (b) and (c)
(iv) all
questions.explanation: PbO loses oxygen (reduced); C gains oxygen (oxidised to CO₂). Statements (a) and (b) are incorrect.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question:
Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe
The above reaction is an example of a
options: combination reaction
double displacement reaction
decomposition reaction
displacement reaction
questions.explanation: Aluminium displaces iron from iron(III) oxide — a displacement (thermit-type) reaction.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
options: To increase its weight before burning
To remove the oxide layer so it burns readily
To make it shine for observation only
To convert it to magnesium oxide first
questions.explanation: Magnesium ribbon is cleaned with sandpaper to remove the oxide coating that would otherwise slow reaction with oxygen.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: Is Mg + O₂ → MgO a balanced chemical equation?
options: Yes, atoms are equal on both sides
No, oxygen atoms are not equal
No, magnesium atoms are not equal
It is a physical change equation
questions.explanation: Left side has 2 O atoms in O₂ but only 1 O in MgO — the equation is unbalanced until written as 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ releases heat. This reaction is best described as
options: endothermic combination
exothermic combination
decomposition
double displacement
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide and water combine to form a single product (slaked lime) with release of heat — exothermic combination.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: When an iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution, the solution turns pale green because
options: iron dissolves without reaction
Fe²⁺ ions replace Cu²⁺ in solution
copper oxidises iron to rust
water evaporates from the solution
questions.explanation: Fe displaces Cu from CuSO₄ forming FeSO₄ (pale green); copper metal deposits on the nail.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is reduced?
options: H₂
CuO
H₂O
Cu
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen and is reduced to Cu; H₂ is oxidised to H₂O.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Reactants and products**?
options: Mg + O₂ → MgO (combination reaction).
Burning Mg gives magnesium oxide.
Left side = reactants; right side = products
New substance + new properties → chemical change.
questions.explanation: Left side = reactants; right side = products.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Chemical Reactions Around Us · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Chemical reactions everywhere**?
options: Heat change often accompanies chemical reactions.
Chemistry is not only in the lab
Remove surface oxide before heating.
Signs → equations → types → redox → corrosion/rancidity.
questions.explanation: Chemistry is not only in the lab.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Chemical Reactions Around Us · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **What is a chemical reaction?**?
options: Many reactions release heat (exothermic); some absorb heat (endothermic).
Clean Mg ribbon burns with dazzling white flame; white powdery ash (MgO) forms.
Record what you see: flame colour, smoke, residue colour, temperature change.
A chemical reaction is a process in which one or more substances change into new substances with different properties.
questions.explanation: New substances form in a chemical reaction.
questions.category_label: Day 1 — Chemical Reactions Around Us · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron filings? Tick the correct answer.
options: Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced.
Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced.
No reaction takes place.
Iron salt and water are produced.
questions.explanation: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂ — hydrogen gas evolves and iron(II) chloride forms.
questions.chapter_ref: NCERT Class 10 Ch 1 — Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Law of conservation of mass**?
options: Exam full marks: balanced + states.
Trial coefficients systematically.
Atoms rearrange; total mass stays same
Only coefficients change; formulae stay fixed.
questions.explanation: Atoms rearrange; total mass stays same.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Balanced Equations & Conservation of Mass · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Lavoisier's contribution**?
options: Exam full marks: balanced + states.
Same atoms each side — nothing created or destroyed.
Conservation of mass → must balance equations
Atoms rearrange; total mass stays same.
questions.explanation: Conservation of mass → must balance equations.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Balanced Equations & Conservation of Mass · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Balanced chemical equation**?
options: Unbalanced equation violates conservation of mass; exam answers must be balanced unless asked otherwise.
2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s) — two Mg and two O on each side.
If gas escapes (CO₂, H₂), mass of open system appears to decrease — still conserved in universe.
Balanced equation has equal number of atoms of each element on both sides.
questions.explanation: Same atoms each side — nothing created or destroyed.
questions.category_label: Day 5 — Balanced Equations & Conservation of Mass · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Start with complex molecule**?
options: Show balanced equation clearly.
Often already balanced — still verify.
Fix big molecule coefficient first
Clear fractions in final answer.
questions.explanation: Fix big molecule coefficient first.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Balancing Chemical Equations · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Balance hydrogen and oxygen last**?
options: 30 seconds verification saves marks.
LCM trick for O atoms: 6 each side.
Save O₂ coefficient for the end
Clear fractions in final answer.
questions.explanation: Save O₂ coefficient for the end.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Balancing Chemical Equations · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Hit-and-trial balancing — steps**?
options: Write formulae → count atoms → change coefficients → recount until balanced.
H and O often appear in multiple products — balance other elements first.
Begin balancing with the compound containing most atoms (often largest formula).
If stuck, use fractional coefficients temporarily, then multiply all by denominator.
questions.explanation: Repeat until every element matches.
questions.category_label: Day 6 — Balancing Chemical Equations · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Combination — carbon and oxygen**?
options: CO₂ is single product
Count products: exactly one main product.
Two elements → one compound.
Combustion = combination with O₂.
questions.explanation: CO₂ is single product.
questions.category_label: Day 7 — Combination Reactions · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Quick lime and water**?
options: Combination often exothermic, not always.
CaO (quick lime) + water → slaked lime
Rusting is oxidation + combination over time.
CO₂ is single product.
questions.explanation: CaO (quick lime) + water → slaked lime.
questions.category_label: Day 7 — Combination Reactions · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Combination reaction definition**?
options: Calcium oxide reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) — exothermic.
Many combination reactions release heat — CaO + H₂O, burning Mg.
Two or more substances combine to form a single product — A + B → AB.
Carbon burns in oxygen to form carbon dioxide: C + O₂ → CO₂.
questions.explanation: Many reactants → one product.
questions.category_label: Day 7 — Combination Reactions · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Reactivity series role**?
options: Cu more reactive than Ag.
Higher metal kicks out lower metal
Acid reaction is displacement of hydrogen.
Lower metal cannot displace higher.
questions.explanation: Higher metal kicks out lower metal.
questions.category_label: Day 9 — Displacement Reactions · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Iron and copper sulphate**?
options: Cu more reactive than Ag.
Ion colour change indicates displacement.
One element replaced vs ion exchange.
More reactive Fe displaces Cu
questions.explanation: More reactive Fe displaces Cu.
questions.category_label: Day 9 — Displacement Reactions · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Displacement reaction definition**?
options: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu — zinc is more reactive than copper.
More reactive element displaces less reactive element from its compound.
Cu + ZnSO₄ → no reaction — copper less reactive than zinc.
Metal higher in reactivity series displaces metal lower from salt solution.
questions.explanation: Reactivity series decides if displacement occurs.
questions.category_label: Day 9 — Displacement Reactions · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Precipitation reactions**?
options: Double displacement with precipitate.
BaSO₄ white precipitate.
Check valency after swap.
Insoluble product = precipitate reaction
questions.explanation: Insoluble product = precipitate reaction.
questions.category_label: Day 10 — Double Displacement Reactions · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Barium sulphate test**?
options: Exchange: Pb pairs with I, K stays with NO₃.
Acid + base = salt + water.
BaSO₄ white precipitate
Two compounds swap partners.
questions.explanation: BaSO₄ white precipitate.
questions.category_label: Day 10 — Double Displacement Reactions · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Double displacement definition**?
options: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq) — ion exchange.
Exchange of ions between two compounds — AB + CD → AD + CB.
Two compounds react, two products, no single element displacing another → likely double displacement.
Acid + base → salt + water — special double displacement.
questions.explanation: Two compounds swap partners.
questions.category_label: Day 10 — Double Displacement Reactions · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Oxidation definition (hydrogen)**?
options: Reducing agent gets oxidised.
Apply four definitions systematically.
Gain of oxygen = oxidation.
Loss of H counts as oxidation
questions.explanation: Loss of H counts as oxidation.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Reduction definition (oxygen)**?
options: Reducing agent gets oxidised.
Loss of oxygen = reduction
Gain of oxygen = oxidation.
Zn is reducing agent; CuO is oxidising agent.
questions.explanation: Loss of oxygen = reduction.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Oxidation definition (oxygen)**?
options: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: CuO reduced (loses O); H₂ oxidised (gains O as H₂O).
Zn + CuO → ZnO + Cu — Zn oxidised; CuO reduced.
Ask: who gained O or lost H? (oxidised).
Oxidation is gain of oxygen by a substance.
questions.explanation: Gain of oxygen = oxidation.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Rancidity introduction**?
options: Sacrificial protection by zinc.
Antioxidants reduce O₂ attack on fats.
Oxidation of unsaturated fats
Physical barrier stops O₂ and H₂O.
questions.explanation: Oxidation of unsaturated fats.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Oxidation in Everyday Life · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Oxidising agent**?
options: Reducing agent gets oxidised.
Oxidising agent gets reduced
Track O: moves from CuO to H₂.
Loss of oxygen = reduction.
questions.explanation: Oxidising agent gets reduced.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Reducing agent**?
options: Track O: moves from CuO to H₂.
Oxidising agent gets reduced.
Reducing agent gets oxidised
Zn is reducing agent; CuO is oxidising agent.
questions.explanation: Reducing agent gets oxidised.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Reduction definition (hydrogen)**?
options: Reduction is gain of hydrogen by a substance.
Substance that removes oxygen or gives hydrogen — itself gets oxidised.
Substance that gives oxygen or removes hydrogen — itself gets reduced.
Zn + CuO → ZnO + Cu — Zn oxidised; CuO reduced.
questions.explanation: Gain of H counts as reduction.
questions.category_label: Day 11 — Oxidation and Reduction · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Antioxidants in food**?
options: Physical barrier stops O₂ and H₂O.
Antioxidants reduce O₂ attack on fats
Many daily changes involve oxidation.
Less O₂ and lower temperature slow rancidity.
questions.explanation: Antioxidants reduce O₂ attack on fats.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Oxidation in Everyday Life · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Corrosion introduction**?
options: Sacrificial protection by zinc.
Exclude O₂ to slow oxidation.
Metal + environment → damage
Less O₂ and lower temperature slow rancidity.
questions.explanation: Metal + environment → damage.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Oxidation in Everyday Life · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Oxidation in everyday life**?
options: Cold and sealed containers slow oxidation of food fats.
Fats and oils oxidise on exposure to air — smell and taste turn unpleasant.
NCERT section 1.
Food oxidised in body releases energy — slow controlled oxidation.
questions.explanation: Many daily changes involve oxidation.
questions.category_label: Day 12 — Oxidation in Everyday Life · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Rusting of iron**?
options: Barrier method blocks contact.
Needs both O₂ and H₂O
Corrosion weakens structures.
Four-part answer scores well.
questions.explanation: Needs both O₂ and H₂O.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Corrosion · Apply — examples and reasoning

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Conditions for rusting**?
options: Zinc protects even if scratched (partially).
Al oxide layer protects inner metal.
Prevention cheaper than replacement.
Remove O₂ or H₂O to prevent rust
questions.explanation: Remove O₂ or H₂O to prevent rust.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Corrosion · Avoid mistakes — common confusions

questions.question: Which statement best describes **Corrosion definition**?
options: Iron rusts when both oxygen and water (or water vapour) are present.
Coating iron with thin layer of zinc — zinc corrodes first (sacrificial protection).
Corrosion is oxidation of metals by moisture, air, acids, and gases in environment.
Define corrosion → give rust equation → state conditions → list prevention (galvanisation, paint, alloying).
questions.explanation: Corrosion weakens structures.
questions.category_label: Day 13 — Corrosion · Recall — definitions and key facts

questions.question: What is the key takeaway about **Foods prone to rancidity**?
options: Inert gas reduces oxidation rate.
Limit O₂ exposure to prevent.
Cold slows chemical reaction rate.
Unsaturated fats oxidise faster
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fats oxidise faster.
questions.category_label: Day 14 — Rancidity · Apply — examples and reasoning
